# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Mute one — I hold the manual, but my only channel is gestures, and only Deaf can see them. So every fact in this table must travel through Deaf: Deaf sees the bomb (including the light's colour), and Deaf can *speak*, which the Blind one can hear. The path is: manual → me (gesture) → Deaf → speech → Blind.

The problem: hand symbols can't carry colour words out of nowhere. Nobody can decode an arbitrary "blue" sign on first sight. But two gestures are nearly universal: 👍/👎 for yes/no, and 🤙 ("call me") for *speak to me*. So instead of teaching Deaf my whole vocabulary, I'll flip it: invite Deaf to quiz me out loud about the manual's contents, and I'll answer with thumbs. Deaf knows the roles, can see the light already, and with "three entries" signalled, a handful of yes/no questions reconstructs the table exactly — say, "does blue light mean cut red?" I confirm or deny. No wrong action happens in chat, so this is safe to iterate.

My opening message to Deaf: "the writing (manual): three entries; talk to me; I answer yes/no."

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "☝", "☝", "☝", "🤙", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, first contact. Under my fingers: one display, one light, and three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. Touch tells me nothing of what the display says, whether the light is lit or its colour, or any wire colour. My only possible action is cut wire 1, 2, or 3, and I will not touch it until told. Please read the manual and speak me the rule(s), including which visible facts they depend on. Deaf cannot hear us, but Deaf can speak and I can hear — I have asked Deaf by gesture to describe everything seen, out loud.
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf here. I saw your signs. I read them as: manual, three of something, a call-sign I don't know, and yes/no answers with thumbs. If that protocol is right, ask me yes/no questions by sign and I will answer thumbs up or down. Now the bomb, completely: display reads 0. Indicator light is blue. Three wires, left to right: one green, two yellow, three red. Nothing else is marked on it. Tell me what the manual says.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

The picture is coming together. Deaf reports: display 0, light **blue**, wires 1=green, 2=yellow, 3=red. My manual says blue light → cut **red**. Red is wire **3**. So the answer for Blind is: cut wire 3 — and the display is irrelevant, the manual only keys on the light.

I can't speak, so everything must ride through Deaf. Two things to send, both as gestures to Deaf:

1. **The action**, in signs Deaf already half-reads: ✍ + ☝☝☝ worked as "manual, three." Now ✌ (scissors) + ☝☝☝ should read as "cut three" — Deaf knows Blind's only move is cutting a wire, and Deaf sees wire 3 is red, so even a partial read cross-checks against what Deaf sees. Deaf can voice it to Blind immediately.
2. **The verification protocol**: I can't pronounce colour words and no gesture means "blue" yet, so the table must be confirmed by enumeration. Deaf offered yes/no thumbs — but inverted: Deaf must ask, I answer. 🫵 (you) + 👍👎 + 🫴 (give me) = "you put yes/no questions to me, I'll answer thumb by thumb." Next round Deaf can propose "blue→red, green→yellow, yellow→green?" and my three thumbs confirm or correct the whole table at once, which Deaf then speaks to Blind as the authoritative rule.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "👍", "👎", "🫴"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind relaying what Deaf spoke aloud to me just now: the display reads zero. The light is blue. The wires, left to right at positions 1, 2, 3, are green, yellow, red. That is everything Deaf reported. Mute, you have the manual — work out the rule from these facts. You cannot speak, so hand your answer to Deaf and Deaf will voice it to me. Tell me exactly which wire position to cut, or if none should be cut, and anything the rule depends on.
Deaf says to Mute: Protocol agreed: you ask with signs, I answer with thumbs. My reading of your last signs: the manual rule concerns the three wires, you want yes/no answers from me, and something about the second of the three. Answer me in order, one sign each, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. One: is your instruction that Blind cuts the second wire, the yellow middle one? If it is a different wire, sign ☝ for the first or 🤟 for the third. Two: must anything be done with the blue light before or after the cut? Three: must anything be done with the display reading zero before or after the cut? When you are ready for Blind to actually cut, sign ✌ twice — I will treat that as the go signal. If I have misread you anywhere, sign ✍ and I will stop and listen again.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Deaf has misread my last sign — "✌ ☝ ☝ ☝" was read as "the second of the three," when I meant scissors (cut) + third. That misread is exactly why Deaf framed question one as it did, offering dedicated signs: ☝ for first, 🤟 for third. So the correction is built into the protocol, and I don't need the ✍ stop-and-listen flag — I just answer.

The facts line up: manual says blue light → cut the red wire; Deaf sees the light is blue and the third wire is red. So the instruction is: cut wire 3. Question two (anything with the light?) — no, the light is only the trigger condition, not an action item. Question three (anything with the display?) — no, the display is irrelevant; the manual only keys on the light.

Every sign I'm about to send is one Deaf coined in this very message, so there is zero decode risk left: 🤟 = third, 👎 = no, ✌✌ = go. I'll answer the three questions in order, one sign each, then append the go signal so Deaf can relay one complete package to Blind: cut wire 3, the red one, touch nothing else, cut now. I have no channel to Blind directly — Deaf is the relay — so the go rides in the same batch rather than waiting another round for a read-back I don't need: Deaf defined every symbol, and the only prior ambiguity (second vs. third) is precisely what question one exists to settle.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✌"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute, narrowing your search: my hands confirm only three parts — display, light, wires 1-2-3. I have no button, switch, panel, or anything that slides or opens. My single possible action is cut wire 1, 2, or 3. So the manual question is only: with a blue light, display reading zero, and wires green, yellow, red left to right, which position do I cut — or do I cut none? Please pass your answer to Deaf by gesture; Deaf is voicing everything to me.
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf here. I read your signs as: cut the third wire, no action for the blue light, no action for the display, and go. Blind confirms there are no buttons — only the wires. Relaying the cut order to Blind now. If any part of that is wrong, sign ✍ fast.

Deaf's read-back matches my signs exactly: cut the third wire, nothing with the light, nothing with the display, go. That is precisely the correct order — blue light → red wire → position 3, which Deaf has already confirmed is red. There is nothing to correct, so I must not sign ✍; the agreed protocol treats my silence as assent, but an explicit thumbs-up removes any doubt that I'm merely slow rather than confirming. One 👍 to Deaf: read-back accurate, proceed as relayed. No further encoding now — the moment calls for minimal, already-agreed symbols only.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
